name: gambit
why: Game theory solvers for computing Nash equilibria of normal and extensive form games, a real mathematical toolkit you can run at home.

brief.what_it_is: Gambit is a set of software tools for computation on finite, noncooperative games in extensive or strategic form. You construct a game, either by building it or by reading it from a standard file format, and it computes pure and mixed-strategy Nash equilibria. It also computes quantal response equilibria and can fit quantal response models to data. It comes as a GUI for interactive work, command-line tools for scripting, and the pygambit Python package for automating games at scale.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage frames it as the package for computation in game theory, and says the Gambit Project was founded in the mid-1980s at the California Institute of Technology. The GitHub README describes it as the package for doing computation in (non-cooperative) game theory.

commands_seen.context: Installs the Python package pygambit from PyPI (the homepage's Python download line).
Installs the pre-release (dev) version of pygambit from PyPI, as offered in the homepage's Preview section.

brief.install_notes: Homepage download options are Source, macOS, and Windows, plus the Python package. The Python route is pip install pygambit, which needs a working Python and pip. Pre-releases of pygambit come from pip install --pre. Official releases are on the GitHub releases page. The README and homepage mention no accounts, hardware, or first-run configuration. The homepage download list names no Linux binary; Linux users would presumably use the source or pip route, but I did not verify that.
brief.standout: One codebase is offered three ways: a GUI, command-line executables for scripting, and a Python package for solving games at scale. It has also been developed since the mid-1980s at Caltech, and the homepage credits Alan Turing Institute funding for Gambit 17.
brief.status: maintained, with weak evidence. The homepage lists a dev release alongside the stable one, the GitHub repo has a documentation badge and PyPI badges, and the contributor list is active. I did not see a release date or last commit date, and the homepage's 'Latest release: latest' is a placeholder rather than a version number.
brief.caveats: The scope is finite games only; the README does not mention infinite or continuous games. The homepage download list is Source, macOS, and Windows, with no explicit Linux binary. The README does not state a license in text, though the PyPI badge shows one. I did not fetch the full documentation at gambitproject.readthedocs.io, so the CLI details, file formats, and algorithm list are unverified.
quotes: Build, analyse, and explore finite extensive and strategic form games
Gambit is the package for doing computation in (non-cooperative) game theory.
Command-line tools suitable for scripting or calling from other programs
